newsitem.title: RUSSIA: TWO RUSSIA OIL FIRMS SIGN IRAQI DEALS-COORDINATOR.
newsitem.headline: TWO RUSSIA OIL FIRMS SIGN IRAQI DEALS-COORDINATOR.

text.p: Two Russian oil trading firms signed the country's first deals with Iraq to lift crude under the second phase of the U.N. food-for-oil scheme, taking a total of 8.20 million barrels between them, a senior Russian oil source said on Monday.

"Two deals were signed in Baghdad on Saturday," said Yuri Agababov, deputy general director of Zarubezhneft, the Russian trading company coordinating Russian purchases of Iraqi oil. "Zarubezhneft itself signed a deal to lift 5.55 million barrels, and Alfa-Eko another for 2.65 million barrels."
Agababov also said two Russian oil producers, not part of the first phase of the oil-for-food plan, intended to take part in the second phase.
"ONAKO and SIDANKO also want to take part," Agababov said. He said all eight firms involved in the first phase were taking part in the second, taking Russia's total to 10 participants at this stage.

Representatives of about eight Russian firms are currently in Baghdad for talks with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO), Agababov said. He declined to give a forecast of how much oil they would lift overall.

But sources at companies likely to involved in the scheme said Russia was looking to boost the amount of Iraqi oil it lifted from the almost 28.54 million barrels bought under the first 180-day programme.
